   410	def signature(rows: list[dict], occ: dict | None = None) -> str:
   411	    """Stable digest of the ready set and its reasons (no elapsed timers).
   412	
   413	    The occupancy ALARM state joins it — not the live count, which changes every
   414	    minute and would defeat the suppression — so that crossing the floor in
   415	    either direction posts instead of being suppressed as "unchanged".

   448	    except LayerError:

   496	    """Merged PRs since *since*, newest-updated first, one page is enough."""
   497	    rows = gh_common.api("pulls?state=closed&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=100")

   504	        except LayerError:
   505	            continue

   510	                if run_mode.parse_timestamp(merged, "merged_at") >= since:
   511	                    count += 1

   527	def latency_rows(rows: list[dict], merged: int, unexplained: int, ts: str,

   529	    out = [{"ts": ts, "pr": row["pr"], "head": row["head"], "event": "ready",
   530	            "class": row["reason"]["class"], "reason": row["reason"]["detail"],
   531	            "seconds": None, "par": None}
   532	           for row in rows if row["ready"]]
   533	    out.append({"ts": ts, "pr": None, "head": None, "event": "report",
   534	                "class": "summary",
   535	                "reason": f"ready {len(out)}, merged {merged}, unexplained {unexplained}",
   536	                "seconds": None, "par": None})
   537	    if models is not None:
   538	        split = " ".join(f"{name}={count}" for name, count
   539	                         in sorted(models["by_model"].items())) or "none"
   540	        out.append({"ts": ts, "pr": None, "head": None, "event": "models",
   541	                    "class": "summary",
   542	                    "reason": (f"override={models['override']} "
   543	                               f"expected={models['expected'] or 'any'} "
   544	                               f"off_policy={models['off_policy']} {split}"),
   545	                    "seconds": None, "par": None})
   546	    if dead is not None:
   547	        split = " ".join(f"{role}={count}" for role, count
   548	                         in sorted(dead["by_role"].items())) or "none"
   549	        out.append({"ts": ts, "pr": None, "head": None, "event": "dead-sessions",
   550	                    "class": "summary",
   551	                    "reason": f"not-re-dispatched total={dead['total']} {split}",
   552	                    "seconds": None, "par": None})

   559	
   560	def collect(repo_root: Path, cache: Path, now: datetime) -> list[dict]:
   561	    """Every open PR with its readiness and, when ready, its reason."""
   562	    daemon_dir = cache / "watchdog" / "daemon"
   563	    lanes_dir = cache / "watchdog" / "lanes"
   564	    adjudicated = adjudication_list(daemon_dir)
   565	    moved = base_moved_minutes(repo_root, now)
   566	    rows: list[dict] = []
   567	    for pull in gh_common.api("pulls?state=open", paginate=True) or []:
   568	        head = ((pull.get("head") or {}).get("sha")) or ""
   569	        if not head:
   570	            continue
   571	        statuses = gh_common.latest_statuses(head)
   572	        reviews = gh_common.pr_reviews(int(pull["number"]))
   573	        row = readiness(pull, statuses, reviews)
   574	        if row["ready"]:
   575	            number = row["pr"]
   576	            waiting = (number in adjudicated
   577	                       and not has_head_adjudication(number, head))
   578	            row["reason"] = classify_reason(
   579	                row, daemon_dir=daemon_dir, lanes_dir=lanes_dir,
   580	                fresh=head_is_fresh(repo_root, head), base_moved_min=moved,
   581	                adjudicating=waiting, now=now)
   582	        rows.append(row)
   583	    return rows

   587	# CLI
   588	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   589	
   590	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   591	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   592	        prog="ready_report.py", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0],
   593	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
   594	    parser.add_argument("--issue", type=int, help="progress issue (default: run-mode)")
   595	    parser.add_argument("--window-min", type=int, default=60,
   596	                        help="merge-counting window in minutes (default 60)")
   597	    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="post even when unchanged")
   598	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
   599	                        help="print the comment; publish and record nothing")
   600	    args = parser.parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
   601	
   602	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   603	    ts = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
   604	    repo_root = run_mode.repo_root()
   605	    cache = run_mode.cache_root()
   606	    try:
   607	        issue = args.issue
   608	        if issue is None:
   609	            issue = int(run_mode.value_for(run_mode.load_mode(), "progress_issue"))
   610	        rows = collect(repo_root, cache, now)
   611	        merged = merged_in_window(now - timedelta(minutes=args.window_min))
   612	    except LayerError as exc:
   613	        sys.stderr.write(f"ready_report.py: {exc}\n")
   614	        return 2
   615	
   616	    unexplained = sum(1 for row in rows if row["ready"]
   617	                      and row["reason"]["class"] == "unexplained")
   618	    occ = occupancy(cache)
   619	    since = now - timedelta(minutes=args.window_min)
   620	    models = model_census(repo_root, since)
   621	    dead = dead_session_residue(cache, since)
   622	    body = render(rows, merged, window_min=args.window_min, ts=ts,
   623	                  unexplained=unexplained, occ=occ, models=models, dead=dead)
   624	    digest = signature(rows, occ)
   625	    state_file = state_path(cache)
   626	    state = read_state(state_file)
   627	    post, why = should_post(state, digest, merged, now, force=args.force)
   628	
   629	    if args.dry_run:
   630	        sys.stdout.write(body)
   631	        sys.stdout.write(f"\n(dry run: would {'post' if post else 'suppress'} — {why})\n")
   632	        return 0
   633	    if not post:
   634	        sys.stdout.write(f"suppressed: {why}\n")
   635	        return 0
   636	
   637	    marker = f"<!-- {REPORT_MARKER} slot={now.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H')} -->"
   638	    try:
   639	        gh_common.ensure_pr_comment(issue, marker, body)
   640	    except LayerError as exc:
   641	        sys.stderr.write(f"ready_report.py: posting to #{issue} failed: {exc}\n")
   642	        return 2
   643	
   644	    path = latency_path(repo_root, now)
   645	    for record in latency_rows(rows, merged, unexplained, ts, models, dead):
   646	        run_mode.locked_append(path, json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False))
   647	    atomic_write(state_file, json.dumps(
   648	        {"signature": digest, "posted_at": ts, "issue": issue,
   649	         "ready": sum(1 for row in rows if row["ready"]), "merged": merged,
   650	         "unexplained": unexplained,
   651	         "off_policy_models": (models or {}).get("off_policy", 0),
   652	         "dead_not_redispatched": (dead or {}).get("total", 0)}, indent=1) + "\n")
   653	    sys.stdout.write(f"posted on #{issue} ({why}); ready "
   654	                     f"{sum(1 for row in rows if row['ready'])}, merged {merged}, "
   655	                     f"unexplained {unexplained}\n")
   656	    return 0
   657	
   658	
   659	if __name__ == "__main__":
   660	    raise SystemExit(main())

184	## 4. The standing reports
   185	
   186	| Channel | Content | Writer |
   187	|---|---|---|
   188	| Estimate issue (`run.estimate_issue`) | **exactly two lines**: the bold headline and one `<sub>` provenance line; never anything else | `local/bin/estimate_post.py`, called by `owner-tools/estimate.sh` from cron |
   189	| Progress log (`run.progress_issue`) | (a) one five-line progress comment every 30 min in `fast` mode; (b) one hourly readiness report; (c) one line per stage boundary, merge, adopted mathematical correction, automatic PR retirement and repair | (a) and (c) the main session (`local/personas/main.md`, "Standing reports"); (b) `local/bin/ready_report.py` from cron |
   190	| Owner inbox (`run.owner_inbox_issue`) | permission, credential, access or scope grants only; ten plain lines; one id | the main session |
   191	
   192	`estimate_post.py` renders the body from values on the command line and refuses
   193	any other body; there is no way to pass it prose. The issue number comes from
   194	the run mode and was validated at briefing time, so a missing
   195	`watchdog/estimate-issue` can no longer silently no-op the owner's only
   196	progress channel.
   197	
   198	`ready_report.py` implements the owner's rule *"a ready-to-merge PR left open
   199	needs a good reason"*. It computes readiness on the exact head and, for each
   200	ready-but-open PR, reads the reason from daemon state rather than guessing:
   201	`refreshing` (pid, lane, elapsed), a `failed` marker (class and reason string),
   202	`parked` (the lane's `needs-attention` reason), `awaiting-adjudication`,
   203	`stale` (the base moved, minutes since), or `unexplained`. **`unexplained` is
   204	the alarm case and should always be zero.** A post is suppressed when the ready
   205	set and the reasons are unchanged and nothing merged, and forced at least every
   206	six hours. The same rows go to `results/telemetry/merge-latency-<date>.jsonl`.
   207	
   208	The hourly comment also carries two counts the owner would otherwise have to
   209	audit by hand:
   210	
   211	* **models** — sessions started in the window grouped by the model that actually
   212	  ran, next to the override in force and, when the override names one model, the
   213	  number of rows that disagree with it. A full speed run whose reviewers slipped
   214	  onto the cheap model shows up here within the hour; before it existed the only
   215	  check was reading `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` by hand.
   216	* **dead sessions marked failed and NOT re-dispatched, per role** — the janitor's
   217	  residue. `local/bin/janitor.sh` re-dispatches **`reviewer` only**: that is the
   218	  one role whose re-run is a pure re-run of the same work (`review.sh`, the exact
   219	  head, and the new verdict supersedes). A dead prover, orc or fixer is marked
   220	  `failed` with a `residue` field in `watchdog/janitor/actions.jsonl` and is the
   221	  OWNING SESSION'S to re-plan — the janitor does not invent a packet. Widening
   222	  it means giving those roles a re-dispatch entry point first and then listing
   223	  them in `MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REDISPATCH_ROLES`; until then the count is on the
   224	  progress issue so the remainder is visible without opening a file on the host.
   225	
   226	The split between the two issues is normative in
   227	`local/protocols/issues-prs.md` section 6.
   228	
   215	
   216	`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local
   217	location); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read
   218	from the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5) bounds `autofix.sh`'s
   219	own loop only — the merge gate does not read it — and is operator-tunable with
   220	the reason recorded in `results/telemetry/events.md`, unlike
   221	`MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE` (the pre-commit budget), the one owner-gated control
   222	in the layer. `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` and
   223	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).
   224	
   225	`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only
   226	snapshot of open issues and PRs to `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/`
   227	(and, since the push goes through `checked-push.sh`, commits that snapshot and
   228	`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` to the primary checkout so the next publish
   229	finds a clean tree)
   230	(`open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, `metadata.json`; PRs filtered out of the
   231	issue endpoint) — audit and recovery telemetry, never lifecycle input. The
   232	retired trees stay archived under `results/telemetry/registry-archive/` (commit
   233	c8f1999): read-only research data, never edited or read as active input.
   234	
   235	## 6. Owner inbox and mathematical-gap escalation
   236	
   237	Pinned issue #500 is the owner inbox — during a run it is
   238	`run.owner_inbox_issue` in the briefing, read with
   239	`local/bin/run_mode.py get owner_inbox_issue`; the retired #26 is archived and
   240	no longer read. It receives only decisions that require
   241	the human owner: a permission, credential, access or scope grant, in ten plain
   242	lines carrying one id. A source statement found to be mathematically false does
   243	not go there first. Following the availability report on the owner inbox and
   244	the September 6
   245	owner decision, main selects Astra Ultra for the mathematical-gap lane through
   246	`MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6-astra local/bin/dispatch.sh --role mathfix --effort ultra`.
   247	Historical owner-launched Fable measurements remain unchanged. Every request or
   248	dispatch carries the exact source path, label and line range; the counterexample
   249	or obstruction; the paper-gap note; the relevant blueprint dependency graph and
   250	Lean consumers; and the cumulative session count and elapsed working time.
   251	
   252	A correction is adopted only when it meets all four conditions below.
   253	
   254	1. **Correctness:** the known counterexample no longer applies, adversarial
   255	   checks find no replacement counterexample, and a mathematical proof sketch
   256	   derives the corrected conclusion from its explicit hypotheses using cited
   257	   source results.
   258	2. **Sufficiency:** every use in the paper and every dependent node in the
   259	   blueprint graph remains justified; checking only the first Lean consumer is
   260	   insufficient.
   261	3. **Minimality:** the correction is the closest sufficient statement to the
   262	   source, with no unnecessary hypothesis or weakened conclusion and no change
   263	   to the source semantics; definition or game corrections require an explicit
   264	   faithfulness audit and independent mathematical review.
   265	4. **Lean convergence:** the corrected statement type-checks and all affected

I’m checking the remaining reporting and spool paths for the same class of false-success behavior.

   310	`watchdog/max-codex` is the mechanical sum of the per-account caps and has **no
   311	admission meaning**: the router reads only `max-codex-{primary,second}`. It is
   312	kept for the lane runner's internal parallelism and the operator display
   313	(`local/protocols/capacity.md`).
   314	
   315	#### Failure classes
   316	
   317	Every session ending is classified by `telemetry.py classify_failure` over the
   318	captured event stream and recorded on the registry row as `failure_class`, with
   319	`failure_detail`, `failure_endpoint` and `retries_seen` beside it. The provider
   320	wordings are data, not code: `local/capacity-policy.json` may replace the whole
   321	table under `failure_patterns`, so a wording change is a one-file edit.
   322	
   323	| Class | What it means | Retryable |
   324	|---|---|---|
   325	| `none` | exit 0 | — |
   326	| `refused` | the router never admitted the dispatch | yes |
   327	| `endpoint_down` | the dispatcher refused to reserve on an endpoint the controller had marked `down` | yes |
   328	| `concurrency_limit` | `Concurrency limit exceeded for account` | yes |
   329	| `endpoint_5xx` | 503/502/504 from the endpoint | yes |
   330	| `retries_exhausted` | the client gave up reconnecting (`Reconnecting... 5/5`) | yes |
   331	| `timeout` | our own `MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT` guard fired | **no** |
   332	| `task_failure` | a clean nonzero exit with model output — the work failed | **no** |
   333	| `unknown` | anything else | **no** |
   334	
   335	`unknown` is the safe default and the capacity controller treats it as
   336	**neutral**: neither an increase nor a decrease. A provider wording change
   337	therefore degrades to static behaviour instead of collapsing the caps.
   338	When a transient class ends a session that produced **no model turn**, the row's
   339	`status` is `refused`, not `failed`: the dispatch was never admitted, so it is
   340	not scored as a failed attempt against a proof packet's budget.
   341	
   342	#### Key labels and endpoints
   343	
   344	`dispatch.sh` takes the key label and the endpoint for the **selected** account
   345	from the run mode file (`run_mode.py get`, else `watchdog/run-mode.json`), and
   346	passes both to `telemetry.py` for **both** accounts. `MIPSTARRE_KEY_LABEL`
   347	overrides them. A label must match `[a-z0-9.-]{1,40}`; one outside that class
   348	fails the dispatch closed rather than being rewritten to `unknown`, and a label
   349	is never interpolated into a shell command or a path unquoted. `relay-1`,
   350	`space` and `unknown` are inside the class, so historical rows stay valid. Every
   351	row carries an `endpoint`, so a key moved between homes keeps the identity that
   352	failures and health are attributed to.
   353	
   354	#### Endpoint preflight, spool and retry
   355	
   356	Before reserving, `dispatch.sh`:
   357	
   358	1. **refuses a `down` endpoint.** `watchdog/capacity/health-<account>.json` is
   359	   written by the capacity controller; its absence means healthy. A retry
   360	   against a `down` account waits for half-open instead of firing — five
   361	   client-side retries against a dead endpoint are exactly how 69 refusals
   362	   became 69 deaths on 2026-09-12.
   363	2. **claims the branch** (below).
   364	3. **spools the request** to `watchdog/capacity/spool/<name>.json`: role, issue,
   365	   PR, worktree, branch, persona ref, effort, job class, sandbox, the prompt
   366	   file path, the attempt count and the deadline. The prompt is copied beside
   367	   it, so the janitor can replay the exact dispatch.
   368	
   369	A `refused` / `endpoint_down` / `concurrency_limit` / `endpoint_5xx` /
   370	`retries_exhausted` outcome is **not** a death: the dispatcher sleeps a jittered
   371	exponential backoff (base 30 s, cap 10 min) and re-reserves, up to
   372	`MIPSTARRE_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS` (default 5) or the run's dispatch cutoff
   373	(`run.dispatch_cutoff`; the literal `until my word` means none). When those run
   374	out it exits **7** and leaves the spool entry for the janitor. A router refusal
   375	is therefore a retryable condition of the day, not a preflight death.
   376	
   377	Two rules on that retry are load-bearing:
   378	
   379	- **A transient-class retry never consumes a proof packet attempt** and never
   380	  resets a budget. The continuation handoff is validated once, before the loop,
   381	  so the `account_router.continuation()` budget fields are untouched; the
   382	  retried dispatch reuses the same session name with an `-a<N>` suffix, so
   383	  telemetry keeps one episode rather than N unrelated sessions.
   384	- **A retry is gated on endpoint health**, per (1) above.
   385	
   386	A successful dispatch clears its spool entry; anything else leaves it.
   387	
   388	#### Branch claim — one writer per branch
   389	
   390	A branch can be checked out in more than one worktree, so the worktree lock is
   600	| worktree | `.worktrees/<branch>` | removed at archival |
   601	| locks | `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` | released at exit |
   602	| branch claim | `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/branch-<branch>.claim` | released at exit; stale pids broken |
   603	| spool entry | `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/capacity/spool/<name>.json` | cleared on delivery; left for the janitor otherwise |
   604	
   605	The registry line schema is in `meta.md`. Beyond it, `dispatch.sh` records
   606	`turns` (completed model turns), `capture` (repo-relative path to the event
   607	stream) and, when resolvable, `rollout`. New dispatches record `account` and the
   608	explicitly resolved `model` as described in §4.1. They also record
   609	`requested_effort` when §4.1 produces a nonempty override; historical rows are
   610	unchanged. Every new row also carries `endpoint`, `failure_class`,
   611	`failure_detail`, `failure_endpoint` and `retries_seen` (§4.1, Failure classes),

   616	`status: done` or `failed` at the end of a run, and `active` is reserved for

   188	| Estimate issue (`run.estimate_issue`) | **exactly two lines**: the bold headline and one `<sub>` provenance line; never anything else | `local/bin/estimate_post.py`, called by `owner-tools/estimate.sh` from cron |
   189	| Progress log (`run.progress_issue`) | (a) one five-line progress comment every 30 min in `fast` mode; (b) one hourly readiness report; (c) one line per stage boundary, merge, adopted mathematical correction, automatic PR retirement and repair | (a) and (c) the main session (`local/personas/main.md`, "Standing reports"); (b) `local/bin/ready_report.py` from cron |
   190	| Owner inbox (`run.owner_inbox_issue`) | permission, credential, access or scope grants only; ten plain lines; one id | the main session |
   191	
   192	`estimate_post.py` renders the body from values on the command line and refuses
   193	any other body; there is no way to pass it prose. The issue number comes from
   194	the run mode and was validated at briefing time, so a missing
   195	`watchdog/estimate-issue` can no longer silently no-op the owner's only
   196	progress channel.
   197	
   198	`ready_report.py` implements the owner's rule *"a ready-to-merge PR left open
   199	needs a good reason"*. It computes readiness on the exact head and, for each
   200	ready-but-open PR, reads the reason from daemon state rather than guessing:
   201	`refreshing` (pid, lane, elapsed), a `failed` marker (class and reason string),
   202	`parked` (the lane's `needs-attention` reason), `awaiting-adjudication`,
   203	`stale` (the base moved, minutes since), or `unexplained`. **`unexplained` is
   204	the alarm case and should always be zero.** A post is suppressed when the ready
   205	set and the reasons are unchanged and nothing merged, and forced at least every
   206	six hours. The same rows go to `results/telemetry/merge-latency-<date>.jsonl`.
   207	
   208	The hourly comment also carries two counts the owner would otherwise have to
   209	audit by hand:
   210	
   211	* **models** — sessions started in the window grouped by the model that actually
   212	  ran, next to the override in force and, when the override names one model, the
   213	  number of rows that disagree with it. A full speed run whose reviewers slipped
   214	  onto the cheap model shows up here within the hour; before it existed the only
   215	  check was reading `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` by hand.
   216	* **dead sessions marked failed and NOT re-dispatched, per role** — the janitor's
   217	  residue. `local/bin/janitor.sh` re-dispatches **`reviewer` only**: that is the
   218	  one role whose re-run is a pure re-run of the same work (`review.sh`, the exact
   219	  head, and the new verdict supersedes). A dead prover, orc or fixer is marked
   220	  `failed` with a `residue` field in `watchdog/janitor/actions.jsonl` and is the
   221	  OWNING SESSION'S to re-plan — the janitor does not invent a packet. Widening
   222	  it means giving those roles a re-dispatch entry point first and then listing
   223	  them in `MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REDISPATCH_ROLES`; until then the count is on the
   224	  progress issue so the remainder is visible without opening a file on the host.

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Which open PRs are ready to merge, and why each ready one has not merged.
     3	
     4	The owner's rule is *"a ready-to-merge PR left open needs a good reason"*.
     5	This is the mechanism for it.  Readiness is computed from GitHub on the exact
     6	head — `local-ci/summary`, `local-review/summary`, unchecked ledger lines in
     7	the marker-bound review, a standing `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, draft — exactly as
     8	`pr_merge.py` gates 1, 3, 4 and 5 read it, and every call goes through
     9	`gh_common.py` (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md` section 1).
    10	
    11	For each ready-but-open PR the reason it has not merged is **read from daemon
    12	state, never guessed**:
    13	
    14	| class | evidence |
    15	|---|---|
    16	| `refreshing` | `watchdog/daemon/pr<N>.refreshing` with a live pid |
    17	| `failed` | `watchdog/daemon/pr<N>.failed`, the daemon's JSON marker (class + reason) |
    18	| `parked` | `watchdog/lanes/<N>.needs-attention` and its recorded reason |
    19	| `awaiting-adjudication` | the PR is on `watchdog/daemon/adj-list` with no exact-head ADJUDICATION comment |
    20	| `stale` | the base moved: `pr_merge.head_is_fresh` is false, with minutes since |
    21	| `unexplained` | ready, fresh, and no daemon record — **the alarm case; it should always be zero** |
    22	
    23	Output: one comment per hour on the run's progress issue in the compact form
    24	``ready N, merged-this-hour M``, one **occupancy** line (live worker sessions
    25	against the briefed floor — the number the owner asked for three times on
    26	2026-09-12 and which nothing measured, because the half-hourly live-vs-floor
    27	line is a main-session duty and a stalled main session reports nothing), one
    28	line per ready-but-open PR with its reason, one **models** line (sessions
    29	started in the window grouped by the model that actually ran, against the
    30	override the run mode has in force — follow-up item W9(5), so a run whose
    31	reviewers slipped onto the cheap model shows up within the hour instead of in a
    32	hand audit of ``sessions.jsonl``), one **dead sessions** line when the janitor
    33	marked sessions ``failed`` without re-dispatching them (it re-dispatches
    34	``reviewer`` only; every other role is the owning session's to re-plan, and that
    35	residue previously existed only in a local report file nothing reads), and the
    36	same rows appended to ``results/telemetry/merge-latency-<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl``.  A post is suppressed
    37	when the ready set and the reasons are unchanged and nothing merged, and forced
    38	at least every six hours.  Elapsed timers are deliberately excluded from the
    39	suppression signature, or nothing would ever be identical.

    41	Usage::

     2	# capacityd.sh — run local/bin/capacity_controller.py tick every 60 s.
     3	# Usage: bash results/telemetry/owner-tools/capacityd.sh [--once]
     4	# Stop it by touching $W/capacity/capacityd.stop (the loop exits within one tick) or by
     5	# killing the pid in $W/capacity/capacityd.pid. This is the whole supervisor: a while/sleep
     6	# loop with a stop file. Anything more is the "hardening the hardening" pattern that cost
     7	# this project 17 hours on 2026-09-01 (design full-speed-v2 §9 item 7).
     8	# A failing tick is logged and retried on the next tick; the controller leaves the cap files
     9	# untouched when its inputs are malformed, so a bad run-mode.json never zeroes capacity.
    10	# Started by results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh --start-loops, by
    11	# owner-resume.sh phase 3, and re-started by the supervising crontab row
    12	# install-crons.sh writes; the run-start runbook in local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md
    13	# §2 names it.  Safe to invoke repeatedly: a second instance exits at the lock.
    14	set -u
    15	export PATH="$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
    16	ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CHECKOUT:-$HOME/MIPStarRE-qpbt}"
    17	W="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}/watchdog"
    18	C="$W/capacity"; STOP="$C/capacityd.stop"; LOG="$C/capacityd.log"; INTERVAL="${CAPACITY_TICK_S:-60}"
    19	mkdir -p "$C" || exit 1
    20	# The stop file is kept across restarts, as the merge daemon's is: the resume path removes it.
    21	[ -e "$STOP" ] && { echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) stop file present; remove $STOP to start" >>"$LOG"; exit 0; }
    22	# Single instance.  The cron row below re-execs this script every few minutes and
    23	# the resume path starts it too; without the lock a run would accumulate one
    24	# controller per start, and two controllers writing the cap files is the one thing
    25	# local/protocols/capacity.md forbids.
    26	exec 9>>"$C/capacityd.lock" || exit 1
    27	if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! flock -n 9; then
    28	  echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) another capacityd holds $C/capacityd.lock; exiting" >>"$LOG"
    29	  exit 0
    30	fi
    31	echo "tool=capacityd.sh version=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown) started $(date -u +%FT%TZ)" >>"$LOG"
    32	echo $$ >"$C/capacityd.pid"
    33	while true; do
    34	  [ -e "$STOP" ] && { echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) stop file present; exiting" >>"$LOG"; break; }
    35	  python3 "$ROOT/local/bin/capacity_controller.py" tick >>"$LOG" 2>&1 ||
    36	    echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) tick failed rc=$? (cap files untouched; retrying in ${INTERVAL}s)" >>"$LOG"
    37	  [ "${1:-}" = "--once" ] && break
    38	  sleep "$INTERVAL"
    39	done
    40	rm -f "$C/capacityd.pid"

     2	"""Retire pull requests whose work is already on ``main`` — mechanically, never by guess.
     3	
     4	On 2026-09-12 PRs 329, 334, 336 and 337 were detected as already merged into
     5	``main`` at 05:37Z and stayed open for three more hours, absorbing refresh lanes
     6	and review re-runs and inflating the ready-but-open count the owner was asked to
     7	interpret.  They were finally closed by hand under an explicit order.  This is
     8	the mechanism that does it, and it closes a PR only when **both** of these hold:
     9

    11	   difference between the merge base and the head: the PR proposes nothing that
    12	   ``main`` does not already have;
    13	2. ``git merge-base --is-ancestor <head> github/main`` succeeds — the head commit
    14	   itself is reachable from ``main``.
    15	
    16	Either condition alone closes nothing.  Condition 1 alone is satisfied by a
    17	branch that adds a commit and reverts it (empty net diff, work never merged);
    18	condition 2 is what proves that *these bytes* are on ``main``.
    19	
    20	What this script must never do, and does not:
    21	
    22	* it never closes an **issue** (that stays with ``pr_merge.py`` and
    23	  ``issue_close.py``; closing the PR leaves the issue open for the work that
    24	  actually carries it);
    25	* it never touches a PR with a nonempty three-dot diff;
    26	* it never acts on a heuristic such as "looks superseded", a title match, an age
    27	  threshold or a label;
    28	* it never converts a GitHub failure into a local success: an error is reported,
    29	  the PR is left open and the next pass retries it.

    32	idempotent PR comment carrying ``<!-- pr-janitor:superseded -->`` that names both
    33	checks and the SHAs, one append-only row in
    34	``$CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/closures.jsonl``, and one bullet in the event log
    35	(``telemetry.py event``).  The hourly report reads the report fragment written by
    36	``--report``.
    37	
    38	This is a PR-only tool and is deliberately distinct from the report-only issue
    39	audits in ``housekeeping.sh``.

    42	    pr_janitor.py [--dry-run] [--pr N]... [--limit N] [--base github/main]
    43	                  [--report PATH] [--no-fetch] [--no-event] [--repo-root PATH]

   236	                    "--repo-root", str(repo_root), "event", "--text", text],
   237	                   capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
   238	
   239	
   240	def process_pull(repo_root: Path, base: str, pull: dict, *, dry_run: bool,
   241	                 write_event: bool) -> dict:
   242	    """Return one result row; never raises for an expected GitHub/git failure."""
   243	    number = int(pull.get("number", 0))
   244	    try:
   245	        evidence = evaluate(repo_root, base, pull)
   246	    except LayerError as error:
   247	        return {"pr": number, "action": "error", "detail": str(error)[:400]}
   248	
   249	    if not evidence["close"]:
   250	        reason = ("diff nonempty" if not evidence["diff_empty"] else
   251	                  "head not reachable from " + base)
   252	        return {"pr": number, "action": "kept", "detail": reason, **evidence}
   253	
   254	    if dry_run:
   255	        return {"pr": number, "action": "would-close", **evidence}
   256	
   257	    try:
   258	        post_marker_comment(number, comment_body(base, evidence))
   259	        close_pull(number)
   260	    except LayerError as error:
   261	        # Reported, not swallowed: the PR stays open and the next pass retries.
   262	        return {"pr": number, "action": "error", "detail": str(error)[:400], **evidence}
   263	
   264	    record_closure(evidence)
   265	    if write_event:
   266	        record_event(repo_root, evidence)
   267	    return {"pr": number, "action": "closed", **evidence}
   268	
   269	
   270	def render_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
   271	    closed = [r for r in rows if r["action"] in ("closed", "would-close")]
   272	    errors = [r for r in rows if r["action"] == "error"]
   273	    lines = [f"pr_janitor: {len(rows)} open PR(s) examined, {len(closed)} superseded, "
   274	             f"{len(errors)} error(s)"]
   275	    for row in closed:
   276	        lines.append(f"  PR {row['pr']} {row['action']}: empty diff against "
   277	                     f"{row.get('base', 'github/main')} and head "
   278	                     f"{str(row.get('head', ''))[:12]} reachable "
   279	                     f"(carried by {str(row.get('carrier', ''))[:12]})")
   280	    for row in errors:
   281	        lines.append(f"  PR {row['pr']} error: {row['detail']}")
   282	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
   283	
   284	
   285	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   286	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
   287	    parser.add_argument("--repo-root", type=Path, default=None)
   288	    parser.add_argument("--base", default=os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_BASE_REF", "github/main"),
   289	                        help="base ref both checks run against (default github/main)")
   290	    parser.add_argument("--pr", type=int, action="append", default=[],
   291	                        help="only consider these PR numbers (repeatable)")
   292	    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0,
   293	                        help="stop after N closures (0 = no limit)")
   294	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
   295	                        help="decide and report; post nothing, close nothing")
   296	    parser.add_argument("--no-fetch", action="store_true",
   297	                        help="do not run git fetch first (the caller just did)")
   298	    parser.add_argument("--no-event", action="store_true",
   299	                        help="do not append an events.md bullet per closure")
   300	    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path,
   301	                        help="write the report fragment here as well as to stdout")
   302	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   303	
   304	    repo_root = (args.repo_root or default_repo_root()).resolve()
   305	    if not (repo_root / "local" / "bin").is_dir():
   306	        parser.error(f"--repo-root {repo_root} is not a checkout (no local/bin)")
   307	
   308	    try:
   309	        if not args.no_fetch:
   310	            fetch(repo_root, args.base.split("/", 1)[0] if "/" in args.base else "github")
   311	        pulls = list_open_pulls()
   312	    except LayerError as error:
   313	        sys.stderr.write(f"pr_janitor: {error}\n")
   314	        return 1
   315	
   316	    if args.pr:
   317	        wanted = set(args.pr)
   318	        pulls = [p for p in pulls if int(p.get("number", 0)) in wanted]
   319	
   320	    rows: list[dict] = []
   321	    closed = 0
   322	    for pull in sorted(pulls, key=lambda p: int(p.get("number", 0))):
   323	        row = process_pull(repo_root, args.base, pull,
   324	                           dry_run=args.dry_run, write_event=not args.no_event)
   325	        rows.append(row)
   326	        if row["action"] in ("closed", "would-close"):
   327	            closed += 1
   328	            if args.limit and closed >= args.limit:
   329	                break
   330	
   331	    report = render_report(rows)
   332	    sys.stdout.write(report)
   333	    if args.report:
   334	        args.report.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   335	        args.report.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
   336	    return 1 if any(row["action"] == "error" for row in rows) else 0
   337	
   338	
   339	if __name__ == "__main__":
   340	    raise SystemExit(main())

     2	# worktree_resolve.sh — resolve the worktree of a branch, registry first.
     3	#
     4	#   local/bin/worktree_resolve.sh [--root DIR] [--create] [--warm] [--quiet] <branch>
     5	#   . local/bin/worktree_resolve.sh   # then call worktree_resolve <branch>
     6	#
     7	# Resolution order, identical to autofix.sh:resolve_worktree and ci.sh:
     8	#   1. `git worktree list --porcelain`, matching `branch refs/heads/<branch>` —
     9	#      git's own registry is the only authority on which directory holds a
    10	#      branch;
    11	#   2. the `.worktrees/<branch>` convention (and the `/`->`-` flattened
    12	#      spelling autofix.sh uses), accepted ONLY when that directory's HEAD is
    13	#      the branch asked for.
    14	#
    15	# A directory that exists but holds a different branch is a MISMATCH and is
    16	# reported as one; it is never used and never silently moved.  On 2026-09-12
    17	# PR 213's lane worktree held a different branch than the PR, so every refresh
    18	# "succeeded" and pushed nothing at all (full-speed-mode v2 design §2 Item 5).
    19	#
    20	# Output: the absolute worktree path on stdout, nothing else.
    21	# Exit: 0 resolved · 2 usage or git failure · 3 mismatch (a path exists for the
    22	#       conventional name but holds another branch) · 4 no worktree (and
    23	#       --create was not given).
    24	set -u
    25	
    26	worktree_resolve() { # <branch> [root] [create] [warm]
    27	  local branch="${1:-}" root="${2:-}" create="${3:-0}" warm="${4:-0}"
    28	  local found flat dest have start
    29	  [ -n "$branch" ] || { printf 'worktree_resolve: branch required\n' >&2; return 2; }
    30	  if [ -z "$root" ]; then
    31	    root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || {
    32	      printf 'worktree_resolve: not a git repository\n' >&2; return 2; }
    33	  fi
    34	  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    35	    printf 'worktree_resolve: %s is not a git repository\n' "$root" >&2; return 2; }
    36	
    37	  found="$(git -C "$root" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
    38	    awk -v b="branch refs/heads/$branch" '
    39	      /^worktree /{ p = substr($0, 10) }
    40	      $0 == b { print p; exit }')"
    41	  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
    42	    printf '%s\n' "$found"
    43	    return 0
    44	  fi
    45	
    46	  flat="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
    47	  for dest in "$root/.worktrees/$branch" "$root/.worktrees/$flat"; do
    48	    [ -e "$dest" ] || continue
    49	    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    50	    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
    51	      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
    52	      return 0
    53	    fi
    54	    printf 'worktree_resolve: %s exists but holds %s, not %s\n' \
    55	      "$dest" "${have:-no git worktree}" "$branch" >&2
    56	    return 3
    57	  done
    58	
    59	  [ "$create" = 1 ] || return 4
    60	
    61	  dest="$root/.worktrees/$branch"
    62	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
    63	  if git -C "$root" show-ref -q --verify "refs/heads/$branch"; then
    64	    git -C "$root" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" || {
    65	      printf 'worktree_resolve: git worktree add %s %s failed\n' "$dest" "$branch" >&2; return 2; }
    66	  else
    67	    start="github/main"
    68	    git -C "$root" show-ref -q --verify "refs/remotes/github/$branch" && start="github/$branch"
    69	    git -C "$root" worktree add --quiet -b "$branch" "$dest" "$start" || {
    70	      printf 'worktree_resolve: git worktree add -b %s %s %s failed\n' "$branch" "$dest" "$start" >&2; return 2; }
    71	  fi
    72	  if [ "$warm" = 1 ] && [ -x "$root/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
    73	    "$root/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
    74	      printf 'worktree_resolve: worktree-setup.sh reported warnings for %s\n' "$dest" >&2
    75	  fi
    76	  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
    77	  return 0
    78	}
    79	
    80	# Sourced: export the function only.  Executed: parse the flags.
    81	if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "${0}" ]; then
    82	  ROOT=""; CREATE=0; QUIET=0; WARM=0; BRANCH=""
    83	  while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    84	    case "$1" in
    85	      --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift ;;
    86	      --create) CREATE=1 ;;
    87	      --warm) WARM=1 ;;
    88	      --quiet) QUIET=1 ;;
    89	      -h|--help) sed -n '2,23p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    90	      --) shift; BRANCH="${1:-}" ;;
    91	      -*) printf 'worktree_resolve.sh: unknown option %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    92	      *) BRANCH="$1" ;;
    93	    esac
    94	    shift || true
    95	  done
    96	  [ -n "$BRANCH" ] || { printf 'usage: worktree_resolve.sh [--root DIR] [--create] [--warm] <branch>\n' >&2; exit 2; }
    97	  if [ "$QUIET" = 1 ]; then
    98	    worktree_resolve "$BRANCH" "$ROOT" "$CREATE" "$WARM" 2>/dev/null
    99	  else
   100	    worktree_resolve "$BRANCH" "$ROOT" "$CREATE" "$WARM"
   101	  fi
   102	  exit $?
   103	fi
     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Guard against Lean modules that no re-export file imports.
     3	
     4	``lake build`` compiles the import closure of the library roots and nothing
     5	else.  A module outside that closure type checks under ``lake env lean`` and
     6	still gets no ``.olean``, so the per-file pre-push gate fails on it in a lane
     7	hours after the merge.  On 2026-09-12 exactly that happened:
     8	``MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points.lean`` did not import its split-out children
     9	``Points.Absorption`` and ``Points.MarginalContraction``, every lane's gate
    10	failed, and the lane runner grew three hand-patched revisions before anyone
    11	looked at the import graph.  This turns it into a CI failure on the PR.
    12	
    13	It is a pure reachability check over import headers, and only that:
    14	
    15	* it NEVER edits a file — re-exports are serialized by the operator and workers
    16	  are told not to touch ``MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean``, so this prints the exact line
    17	  to add and the file to add it to, and stops;
    18	* it reads no proof, no statement, no axiom, no declaration body;
    19	* it has no opinion about whether a module should exist.
    20	
    21	Roots: ``MIPStarRE.lean`` and every ``MIPStarRE/<Name>.lean`` that shadows a
    22	``MIPStarRE/<Name>/`` directory (today ``LDT``, ``QPBT``, ``Quantum``) — the
    23	re-export files AGENTS.md requires to be preserved.  A DEEPER re-export file is
    24	deliberately not a root: unimported, it yields no oleans for its whole subtree,
    25	which is the failure being guarded against.  ``*/Test/*`` modules are excluded
    26	from the walk and are not roots.  Full protocol: ``local/protocols/ci.md`` §7.1.
    27	
    28	Usage::
    29	
    30	    python3 scripts/check_umbrella_imports.py --root . [--ci] [--warn-only]
    31	
    32	Exit status: 0 clean (or ``--warn-only``), 1 findings, 2 the root is not a
    33	MIPStarRE worktree.
    34	"""
    35	
    36	from __future__ import annotations
    37	
    38	import argparse
    39	import sys
    40	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    41	from pathlib import Path
    42	
    43	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    44	# Constants
    45	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    46	
    47	LIB_DIR_NAME: str = "MIPStarRE"
    48	
    49	# Matched against the path parts relative to the repository root.
    50	EXCLUDE_DIRS: tuple[str, ...] = (".git", ".lake", ".worktrees", "lake-packages", "tmp")
    51	
    52	# A directory component with this name marks a test target ("*/Test/*").
    53	TEST_DIR_NAME: str = "Test"
    54	
    55	EXIT_OK: int = 0
    56	EXIT_FINDINGS: int = 1
    57	EXIT_USAGE: int = 2
    58	
    59	
    60	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    61	# Model
    62	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    63	
    64	
    65	@dataclass
    66	class Module:
    67	    """One ``.lean` file, reduced to the only thing this check reads."""
    68	
    69	    name: str  # MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Points
    70	    rel: str  # MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points.lean
    71	    path: Path
    72	    is_test: bool
    73	    imports: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    74	
    75	
    76	@dataclass
    77	class Report:
    78	    """Everything the walk found; rendering and exit status are derived."""
    79	
    80	    root: Path
    81	    roots: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    82	    modules: dict[str, Module] = field(default_factory=dict)
    83	    reachable: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    84	    test_reachable: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    85	    unreachable: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    86	    primary: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    87	    fixed_by: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    88	    targets: dict[str, str | None] = field(default_factory=dict)
    89	    unreadable: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    90	    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    91	
    92	    @property
    93	    def clean(self) -> bool:
    94	        return not self.unreachable and not self.unreadable
    95	
    96	
    97	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    98	# Walking
    99	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   100	
   101	
   102	def _is_excluded(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
   103	    """Return True if *path* is not a ``.lean`` file under a scanned directory."""
   104	
   105	    if path.suffix != ".lean":
   106	        return True
   107	    try:
   108	        rel_parts = path.relative_to(root).parts
   109	    except ValueError:
   110	        return True
   111	    return any(part in EXCLUDE_DIRS for part in rel_parts)
   112	
   113	
   114	def module_name(root: Path, path: Path) -> str:
   115	    """``MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points.lean`` -> ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Points``."""
   116	
   117	    rel = path.relative_to(root)
   118	    return ".".join(rel.with_suffix("").parts)
   119	
   120	
   121	def is_test_module(root: Path, path: Path) -> bool:
   122	    """Return True for ``*/Test/*`` modules (excluded from the walk and from the roots)."""
   123	
   124	    rel = path.relative_to(root)
   125	    return TEST_DIR_NAME in rel.parts[:-1]
   126	
   127	
   128	def iter_lean_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
   129	    """Return every scanned ``.lean`` file: ``MIPStarRE.lean`` plus ``MIPStarRE/**``."""
   130	
   131	    found: list[Path] = []
   132	    top = root / f"{LIB_DIR_NAME}.lean"
   133	    if top.is_file():
   134	        found.append(top)
   135	    lib_dir = root / LIB_DIR_NAME
   136	    if lib_dir.is_dir():
   137	        for path in lib_dir.rglob("*.lean"):
   138	            if path.is_file() and not _is_excluded(path, root):
   139	                found.append(path)
   140	    return sorted(found)
   141	
   142	
   143	def strip_comments(line: str, depth: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
   144	    """Remove Lean comments from one header line.
   145	
   146	    ``depth`` is the nesting depth of ``/- ... -/`` carried in from the previous
   147	    line; the updated depth is returned.  ``--`` ends the line.  Deliberately
   148	    simple: this only ever runs over an import header, where there are no string
   149	    literals to confuse it.
   150	    """
   151	
   152	    out: list[str] = []
   153	    i = 0
   154	    size = len(line)
   155	    while i < size:
   156	        if depth > 0:
   157	            if line.startswith("-/", i):
   158	                depth -= 1
   159	                i += 2
   160	            elif line.startswith("/-", i):
   161	                depth += 1
   162	                i += 2
   163	            else:
   164	                i += 1
   165	            continue
   166	        if line.startswith("/-", i):
   167	            depth += 1
   168	            i += 2
   169	            continue
   170	        if line.startswith("--", i):
   171	            break
   172	        out.append(line[i])
   173	        i += 1
   174	    return "".join(out), depth
   175	
   176	
   177	def parse_imports(text: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   178	    """Return the module names imported by *text*.
   179	
   180	    Lean 4 puts every ``import`` before the first command, with only comments
   181	    (and an optional ``prelude``) interleaved, so the scan stops at the first
   182	    real command.  That keeps an ``import`` word inside a docstring or a proof
   183	    from being mistaken for an import.
   184	    """
   185	
   186	    imports: list[str] = []
   187	    depth = 0
   188	    for raw in text.splitlines():
   189	        visible, depth = strip_comments(raw, depth)
   190	        stripped = visible.strip()
   191	        if not stripped:
   192	            continue
   193	        if stripped == "prelude":
   194	            continue
   195	        if stripped == "import" or stripped.startswith("import "):
   196	            rest = stripped[len("import") :].strip()
   197	            if rest:
   198	                imports.append(rest.split()[0])
   199	            continue
   200	        break
   201	    return tuple(imports)
   202	
   203	
   204	def read_lean(path: Path) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, str | None]:
   205	    """Return ``(text, unreadable_reason, decode_warning)``; never raises."""
   206	
   207	    try:
   208	        raw = path.read_bytes()
   209	    except OSError as exc:  # permissions, a dangling symlink, a vanished file
   210	        return None, str(exc), None
   211	    try:
   212	        return raw.decode("utf-8"), None, None
   213	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
   214	        # Import lines are ASCII, so a replacement character in a docstring
   215	        # cannot change the import graph.  Report it and carry on.
   216	        return raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), None, f"not valid UTF-8 ({exc.reason})"
   217	
   218	
   219	def collect_modules(root: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Module], list[tuple[str, str]], list[str]]:
   220	    """Walk the tree.  Returns ``(modules, unreadable, warnings)``."""
   221	
   222	    modules: dict[str, Module] = {}
   223	    unreadable: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
   224	    warnings: list[str] = []
   225	
   226	    for path in iter_lean_files(root):
   227	        rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   228	        name = module_name(root, path)
   229	        text, unreadable_reason, decode_warning = read_lean(path)
   230	        if text is None:
   231	            unreadable.append((rel, unreadable_reason or "unknown error"))
   232	            continue
   233	        if decode_warning:
   234	            warnings.append(f"{rel}: {decode_warning}; parsed with replacement characters")
   235	        modules[name] = Module(
   236	            name=name,
   237	            rel=rel,
   238	            path=path,
   239	            is_test=is_test_module(root, path),
   240	            imports=parse_imports(text),
   241	        )
   242	    return modules, unreadable, warnings
   243	
   244	
   245	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   246	# Reachability
   247	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   248	
   249	
   250	def reexport_roots(root: Path, modules: dict[str, Module]) -> list[str]:
   251	    """Return the re-export roots: ``MIPStarRE`` and every depth-1 directory shadow."""
   252	
   253	    roots: list[str] = []
   254	    if LIB_DIR_NAME in modules and not modules[LIB_DIR_NAME].is_test:
   255	        roots.append(LIB_DIR_NAME)
   256	    lib_dir = root / LIB_DIR_NAME
   257	    if lib_dir.is_dir():
   258	        for entry in sorted(lib_dir.iterdir()):
   259	            if not entry.is_dir() or entry.name in EXCLUDE_DIRS:
   260	                continue
   261	            shadow = f"{LIB_DIR_NAME}.{entry.name}"
   262	            module = modules.get(shadow)
   263	            if module is not None and not module.is_test and shadow not in roots:
   264	                roots.append(shadow)
   265	    return roots
   266	
   267	
   268	def closure(modules: dict[str, Module], starts: list[str]) -> set[str]:
   269	    """Transitive import closure of *starts*, restricted to known modules."""
   270	
   271	    seen: set[str] = set()
   272	    stack = [name for name in starts if name in modules]
   273	    while stack:
   274	        name = stack.pop()
   275	        if name in seen:
   276	            continue
   277	        seen.add(name)
   278	        for imported in modules[name].imports:
   279	            if imported in modules and imported not in seen:
   280	                stack.append(imported)
   281	    return seen
   282	
   283	
   284	def reexport_file_for(
   285	    name: str,
   286	    modules: dict[str, Module],
   287	    forbidden: set[str] | None = None,
   288	) -> str | None:
   289	    """Return the rel path of the re-export file *name* belongs in.
   290	
   291	    The nearest existing ancestor module: ``…Combining.Points.Absorption`` goes
   292	    into ``MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points.lean`` when that file exists, else
   293	    into ``MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining.lean``, else into ``MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean``.
   294	
   295	    An ancestor in *forbidden* — the modules *name* already imports, directly or
   296	    transitively — is skipped: importing it back would be an import cycle and
   297	    Lake would refuse the build.  When a file was split out of its parent and
   298	    still imports it, the fix therefore climbs to the next re-export file up.
   299	    """
   300	
   301	    blocked = forbidden or set()
   302	    parts = name.split(".")
   303	    for cut in range(len(parts) - 1, 0, -1):

@@ -114,6 +110,33 @@ log()  { printf '%s: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2; }

+# Resolve the reviewer models ONCE, before any worktree, diff or GitHub work,
+# and die with the policy's own message when it refuses.  The 2026-09-12 run
+# lost every fix session to a rejected model that was only discovered at the
+# dispatcher's preflight, one silent death per session; one loud line here is
+# the whole difference.
+POLICY_MODEL_OUT=""
+policy_model() {
+  # policy_model <requested> <label> — sets POLICY_MODEL_OUT, or dies loudly.

+  MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON, never a bare model
+  (local/protocols/review.md, local/protocols/sessions.md §2)."

+PROSE_MODEL="$POLICY_MODEL_OUT"

+++ b/results/telemetry/owner-tools/install-crons.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,205 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# install-crons.sh — regenerate the operator crontab from the run mode (design §7.5).
+#
+# Why this exists: on 2026-09-12 the crontab was edited three times in sequence by in-place
+# `sed` with no backup, and one of those edits (a `#` inside an `s#...#...#` expression)
+# WIPED it.  This script never edits the live crontab: it reads it, writes a complete new
+# file under $W, installs THAT file, and verifies the result.  It fails if `crontab -l`
+# returns nothing, because that is what a wipe looks like.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   install-crons.sh [--paused] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]
+#   install-crons.sh --restore FILE [--allow-empty]     # install FILE verbatim, guarded
+#
+#   --paused       render the paused schedule: estimate at the slow cadence, readiness
+#                  report off, capacityd restart row off.  (owner-pause.sh phase T+2:00;
+#                  the pause also writes watchdog/capacity/capacityd.stop, so the row
+#                  would refuse anyway — this is the second lock on the same door.)
+#   --dry-run      print the crontab that would be installed; touch nothing.
+#   --allow-empty  accept an empty `crontab -l` (first install on a fresh host only).
+#   --restore F    install F verbatim — no regeneration, no sed.  owner-resume.sh uses this
+#                  with the backup the pause recorded, because un-commenting by `sed` would
+#                  resurrect the watchdog / astra-poll / heartbeat rows that have been
+#                  deliberately commented out since 2026-09-09.
+#
+# Which rows this script owns (they come only from run-mode, never from the live crontab):
+#   estimate        every `run_mode.py get estimate_cadence_min` minutes (30 in fast mode)
+#   readiness       hourly, fixed schedule (see READY_SCHED below)
+#   capacityd       every 5 minutes, re-execing capacityd.sh; the loop takes a lock and a
+#                   second instance exits, so this row is a restart-if-dead supervisor and
+#                   never a second controller.  Without it a controller killed by an OOM or
+#                   a reboot never comes back and the caps freeze where they are.
+#   nudging crons   OFF.  The watchdog / heartbeat / astra-poll rows have been deliberately
+#                   disabled since 2026-09-09 and are written as comments, not as rows.
+# Every other line of the live crontab is carried through verbatim, INCLUDING lines that are
+# commented out: a `#PAUSED-...` row carries the schedule someone will want back, and
+# dropping it loses that schedule everywhere but the backup file.
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 `crontab -l` was empty or the install did not take effect
+set -u
+
+PROG="install-crons.sh"
+CACHE_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
+W="$CACHE_ROOT/watchdog"
+OWNER_BIN="${MIPSTARRE_OWNER_BIN:-$CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin}"
+CRONTAB_BIN="${MIPSTARRE_CRONTAB:-crontab}"
+TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
+
+PAUSED=0; DRY=0; ALLOW_EMPTY=0; RESTORE=""
+while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --paused) PAUSED=1 ;;
+    --dry-run) DRY=1 ;;
+    --allow-empty) ALLOW_EMPTY=1 ;;
+    --restore) RESTORE="${2:-}"; [ -n "$RESTORE" ] || { echo "$PROG: --restore needs a file" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '2,38p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "$PROG: unknown argument '$1'" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+  shift
+done
+
+ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT:-}"
+if [ -z "$ROOT" ] && [ -r "$OWNER_BIN/repo-root" ]; then ROOT="$(cat "$OWNER_BIN/repo-root")"; fi
+if [ -z "$ROOT" ]; then ROOT="$HOME/MIPStarRE-qpbt"; fi
+RUN_MODE="${MIPSTARRE_RUN_MODE:-$ROOT/local/bin/run_mode.py}"
+
+VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^short=//p' "$OWNER_BIN/tools-version" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
+echo "tool=$PROG version=${VERSION:-unreleased}"
+if [ ! -r "$RUN_MODE" ]; then
+  echo "$PROG: warning: no run_mode.py at $RUN_MODE; every schedule falls back to its" >&2
+  echo "$PROG: documented default (estimate 6-hourly, readiness hourly, nudgers off)." >&2
+fi
+
+rm_get() { # rm_get KEY [fallback]; loud when there is no fallback
+  local key="$1" fb="${2-}" out=""
+  out="$(python3 "$RUN_MODE" get "$key" 2>/dev/null)" || out=""
+  out="$(printf '%s' "$out" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')"
+  if [ -n "$out" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out"; return 0; fi
+  if [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; then printf '%s\n' "$fb"; return 0; fi
+  echo "$PROG: run_mode.py get $key produced nothing ($RUN_MODE); refusing to guess" >&2
+  return 1
+}
+
+cron_every() { # cron_every <minutes> -> a 5-field schedule, or nonzero
+  local m="$1" h
+  case "$m" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  [ "$m" -gt 0 ] || return 1
+  if [ "$m" -lt 60 ]; then
+    [ $((60 % m)) -eq 0 ] || return 1
+    printf '*/%s * * * *\n' "$m"; return 0
+  fi
+  [ $((m % 60)) -eq 0 ] || return 1
+  h=$((m / 60))
+  if [ "$h" -eq 24 ]; then printf '0 0 * * *\n'; return 0; fi
+  [ $((24 % h)) -eq 0 ] || return 1
+  printf '0 */%s * * *\n' "$h"; return 0
+}
+
+BEGIN='# BEGIN mipstarre-dev — generated by install-crons.sh from watchdog/run-mode.json; do not edit by hand'
+END='# END mipstarre-dev'
+LOG="$W/cron.log"
+
+# Historical rows this block now owns; they are dropped from the carried-through section so
+# a schedule can never exist twice (the 2026-09-12 crontab kept a 6-hourly estimate row and
+# a 30-minute one at the same time).
+OWNED_RE='(estimate\.sh|ready_report\.py|capacityd\.sh|qpbt-watchdog\.sh|owner-heartbeat-check\.sh|astra-poll\.sh|install-crons\.sh)'
+# ...but only LIVE rows.  A commented-out row is a record, not a schedule: dropping the
+# `#PAUSED-20260909 ...` watchdog / heartbeat / astra-poll lines would delete the original
+# schedules from the live crontab on the first regeneration, leaving them only in a backup.
+carry_through() { # stdin: the live crontab -> stdout: the lines this block does not own
+  awk -v b="$BEGIN" -v e="$END" '
+    index($0, b) == 1 { skip = 1; next }
+    index($0, e) == 1 { skip = 0; next }
+    skip != 1 { print }' \
+  | awk -v owned="${OWNED_RE//\\/\\\\}" '
+    /^[[:space:]]*$/ { next }
+    /^[[:space:]]*#/ { print; next }          # commented rows survive verbatim
+    $0 ~ owned { next }                        # live rows this block regenerates
+    { print }'
+}
+
+mkdir -p "$W"
+
+# distinct from owner-pause.sh's crontab.<ts>.bak, which is the file pause-state.json
+# records and owner-resume.sh restores: an install a second later must not overwrite it
+CUR_FILE="$W/crontab.$TS.install.bak"
+CUR="$("$CRONTAB_BIN" -l 2>/dev/null)"
+if [ -z "$CUR" ] && [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "$PROG: crontab -l returned nothing — refusing to install over an empty crontab." >&2
+  echo "$PROG: if this host really has no crontab yet, re-run with --allow-empty." >&2
+  exit 3
+fi
+
+install_file() { # install_file <path>
+  local f="$1"
+  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then
+    echo "$PROG: [dry-run] would install $f:"; sed 's/^/  | /' "$f"; return 0
+  fi
+  "$CRONTAB_BIN" "$f" || { echo "$PROG: crontab $f failed" >&2; return 3; }
+  local now; now="$("$CRONTAB_BIN" -l 2>/dev/null)"
+  if [ -z "$now" ]; then echo "$PROG: crontab is empty after the install — restore $CUR_FILE" >&2; return 3; fi
+  if ! printf '%s\n' "$now" | diff -q - "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "$PROG: warning: the installed crontab differs from $f (cron may normalise comments)" >&2
+  fi
+  echo "$PROG: installed $(grep -c -v '^[[:space:]]*$' "$f") crontab lines from $f"
+  return 0
+}
+
+if [ "$DRY" -eq 0 ]; then
+  printf '%s\n' "$CUR" > "$CUR_FILE"
+  echo "$PROG: previous crontab backed up verbatim to $CUR_FILE"
+fi
+
+if [ -n "$RESTORE" ]; then
+  [ -r "$RESTORE" ] || { echo "$PROG: cannot read $RESTORE" >&2; exit 2; }
+  if [ ! -s "$RESTORE" ] && [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" -eq 0 ]; then
+    echo "$PROG: $RESTORE is empty; refusing (use --allow-empty)" >&2; exit 3
+  fi
+  install_file "$RESTORE"; exit $?
+fi
+
+SPEED="$(rm_get speed default)"
+CADENCE_FB=360; [ "$SPEED" = fast ] && CADENCE_FB=30
+CADENCE="$(rm_get estimate_cadence_min "$CADENCE_FB")"
+[ "$PAUSED" -eq 1 ] && CADENCE=360
+EST_SCHED="$(cron_every "$CADENCE")" || {
+  echo "$PROG: estimate_cadence_min=$CADENCE is not expressible as a cron schedule" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Not run-mode knobs: these two schedules are fixed policy, not per-run numbers the owner
+# briefs.  An environment override exists for tests; there is deliberately no brief field,
+# so nothing here silently falls back to a default while claiming to read the brief.
+READY_SCHED="${MIPSTARRE_READY_CRON:-17 * * * *}"
+CAPD_SCHED="${MIPSTARRE_CAPACITYD_CRON:-*/5 * * * *}"
+[ "$PAUSED" -eq 1 ] && READY_SCHED=off
+[ "$PAUSED" -eq 1 ] && CAPD_SCHED=off
+
+NEW="$W/crontab.$TS.new"
+{
+  # everything the block does not own, verbatim and in order (comments included)
+  printf '%s\n' "$CUR" | carry_through
+  printf '%s\n' "$BEGIN"
+  printf '# release %s · speed=%s%s · regenerate with install-crons.sh, never by hand\n' \
+    "${VERSION:-unreleased}" "$SPEED" "$([ "$PAUSED" -eq 1 ] && printf ' (paused)')"
+  printf '%s %s >> %s 2>&1\n' "$EST_SCHED" "$OWNER_BIN/estimate.sh" "$LOG"
+  if [ "$READY_SCHED" = off ]; then
+    printf '# readiness report: off (paused)\n'
+  else
+    printf '%s cd %s && python3 local/bin/ready_report.py >> %s 2>&1\n' "$READY_SCHED" "$ROOT" "$LOG"
+  fi
+  # capacityd restart-if-dead.  capacityd.sh takes a lock and a second instance exits, so
+  # this row can never start a second controller; it only brings one back after a kill.
+  if [ "$CAPD_SCHED" = off ]; then
+    printf '# capacity controller: off (paused)\n'
+  else
+    printf '%s [ -e %s/capacity/capacityd.stop ] || { setsid %s >> %s 2>&1 < /dev/null & }\n' \
+      "$CAPD_SCHED" "$W" "$OWNER_BIN/capacityd.sh" "$LOG"
+  fi
+  # The nudging crons have been deliberately off since 2026-09-09 (events.md); they are
+  # written as comments so the crontab says so rather than staying silent about them.
+  printf '# qpbt-watchdog.sh: off since 2026-09-09 (deliberate)\n'
+  printf '# owner-heartbeat-check.sh: off since 2026-09-09 (deliberate)\n'
+  printf '# astra-poll.sh: off since 2026-09-09 (deliberate)\n'
+  printf '%s\n' "$END"
+} > "$NEW"
+
+install_file "$NEW"
+exit $?

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# install.sh — the ONE deployment path for the operator tools (design full-speed-v2 §7).
+#
+# Operator scripts drive tmux, the crontab and the host process table, so they cannot be
+# run from the checkout (which is mid-merge for minutes at a time).  They are therefore
+# COPIED to ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/ by this installer and never edited on the
+# host: on 2026-09-12 three versions of the lane runner ran at once, `merge-daemon-v9h.sh`
+# called a `/tmp/merge-v2.sh` that does not exist, and the shim was patched by an
+# `assert old in s` here-doc against a 90-character substring.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   install.sh [--force] [--compat-tmp] [--crons] [--start-loops] [--dry-run]
+#   install.sh --verify                 # dependency/hash check (the merge daemon's gate)
+#   install.sh --record <name>          # re-record a regenerated file (run_mode.py set speed)
+#
+# Options:
+#   --force        overwrite a deployed copy whose hash matches no released version.
+#                  The previous copy is MOVED to owner-bin/attic/<ts>/, never deleted.
+#   --start-loops  start capacityd.sh (the 60 s capacity controller loop) if it is not
+#                  already running and no stop file holds it.  Without a running
+#                  controller nothing writes watchdog/max-codex-*, the caps stay frozen
+#                  at whatever seeded them, there is no AIMD, no 5xx trip and no
+#                  half-open probe — the 2026-09-12 situation, recovered by hand — and on
+#                  a fresh host lane.sh:wait_for_slot fails closed with
+#                  `no-capacity-record`.  The merge daemon and the goal keeper are NOT
+#                  started here: owner-resume.sh owns those (design §5).
+#   --compat-tmp   create /tmp/<name> SYMLINKS into owner-bin/ so anything still invoking
+#                  a historical /tmp path runs versioned code.  Nothing is ever written or
+#                  edited in /tmp; an existing regular file there is refused, not clobbered.
+#   --crons        run install-crons.sh afterwards (crontab regenerated from run-mode).
+#   --dry-run      print the plan and touch nothing (implies --dry-run for --crons too).
+#   --dest DIR     install into DIR instead of $MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin (tests).
+#   --compat-dir D create the compat symlinks in D instead of /tmp (tests).
+#   --speed S      render the PATH shim for speed S instead of asking run_mode.py (tests).
+#
+# What is written under owner-bin/:
+#   <tool>              the deployed copy, mode from the table below
+#   tools-version       describe= sha= short= installed_at= source= installer=  (one release)
+#   manifest.sha256     "<sha256>  <name>" for every file deployed now (sha256sum format)
+#   manifest.accepted   every hash this release accepts for a name; the PATH shim has two
+#                       (the fast and the default rendering), because run_mode.py set speed
+#                       regenerates it in place
+#   repo-root           the checkout this release was installed from
+#   attic/<ts>/         the previous copy of every file this run replaced, plus its manifest
+#
+# Refusal rule (the point of the installer): a deployed file whose hash is neither the
+# incoming one, nor the manifest row, nor an accepted variant, nor a hash recorded in an
+# attic manifest, is a HAND PATCH.  It is reported and the install stops with exit 4.
+# --force is the only way past, and it keeps the patch in the attic.
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 --verify found a missing file or a hash mismatch ·
+#             4 a hand patch was refused · 5 a required source file is missing
+set -euo pipefail
+
+PROG="install.sh"
+
+usage() { sed -n '2,52p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+
+FORCE=0; COMPAT=0; CRONS=0; DRY=0; VERIFY=0; RECORD=""; START_LOOPS=0
+DEST=""; SPEED=""; COMPAT_DIR="${MIPSTARRE_COMPAT_DIR:-/tmp}"
+while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --force) FORCE=1 ;;
+    --compat-tmp) COMPAT=1 ;;
+    --crons) CRONS=1 ;;
+    --start-loops) START_LOOPS=1 ;;
+    --dry-run) DRY=1 ;;
+    --verify) VERIFY=1 ;;
+    --record) RECORD="${2:-}"; [ -n "$RECORD" ] || { echo "$PROG: --record needs a tool name" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
+    --dest) DEST="${2:-}"; [ -n "$DEST" ] || { echo "$PROG: --dest needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
+    --compat-dir) COMPAT_DIR="${2:-}"; [ -n "$COMPAT_DIR" ] || { echo "$PROG: --compat-dir needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
+    --speed) SPEED="${2:-}"; [ -n "$SPEED" ] || { echo "$PROG: --speed needs fast or default" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "$PROG: unknown argument '$1'" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+  shift
+done
+
+CACHE_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
+DEST="${DEST:-$CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin}"
+TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
+
+# --- the checkout this installer belongs to --------------------------------------------
+# When install.sh is run from owner-bin (--verify / --record on the host) it cannot derive
+# the checkout from its own path, so fall back to the recorded repo-root.
+SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+ROOT=""
+if [ -f "$SELF_DIR/../../../AGENTS.md" ]; then
+  ROOT="$(cd "$SELF_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
+elif [ -n "${MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+  ROOT="$MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT"
+elif [ -r "$DEST/repo-root" ]; then
+  ROOT="$(cat "$DEST/repo-root")"
